findings.action: Require the adopted explicit-close contract for an aggregate's own approved verification. The own.Approved early return bypasses the new receipt-aware projection. computeReviewVerification uses scopeLifecycleDone and reports closed at lines 3736-3740 when all milestone members are done, even before a receipt exists. This affects required and voluntary aggregate approvals and disagrees with GetCloseoutState.CloseRequired. Preserve approval while reporting ready-to-close until the applicable closeout receipt stands.

Preserve child standing and applicable blockers when projecting an exemption. The replacement verification discards own.Blockers; receiptStandsFor checks members and exit-gate identity but does not verify member reviews. An exempt milestone with an existing receipt can therefore report closed after a member is rejected. The roadmap branch similarly accepts child receipts at line 3520 without checking whether their reviews and children still stand. Local federated acceptance does not substitute for local spec review verification. Derive closure without suppressing child failures, using a non-recursive projection where necessary.

Finish canonical member resolution in review planning and lifecycle verification. reviewScopeSpecs still calls milestoneMember and GetSpec on the original transferred source, so component selection and observed paths can come from the redirect stub instead of the canonical destination. scopeLifecycleDone in review_closeout.go:2555-2567 also reads the source and requires status done, although transfer leaves it superseded. Consequently an aggregate's approved verification can remain ready-to-close after canonical destination acceptance and explicit close. Use consistent canonical resolution in these remaining consumers and cover preparation plus post-close verification.
